question: When sprites go in front of the scenery, which figures did the original draw behind it, and which only brush a wall?
summary: Use in design (PLAYBOOK 3) before moving figures in front of scenery, for a game whose plotter decides depth per 8x8 cell (an owner map, a scenery-cell test).

question: Which buffer and producer create the figure before the final screen copy?
summary: Producer and consumer share the observed mapped memory view.

question: Which live registers, stack values and memory fields describe a draw?
summary: Capture a small set of live drawing parameters when static bytes or caller inspection leave the drawing interface uncertain.

question: Would removing a figure from the ULA change what the game decides?
summary: Find every read of a screen byte that holds figure pixels and decide whether the result depends on the figure.

question: How are graphics dimensions, mask flags and record boundaries encoded?
summary: Establish the layout of graphics records when a known source region cannot yet be decoded reliably.

question: Where does the original wait, how much usable time is left per update, and does the code hooks would touch also play sound?
summary: First step for an unknown engine, before any hook budget is set (PLAYBOOK 3d: an assumed amount of spare time is no budget).

question: If the original routine is skipped, does anything the game later decides change?
summary: Run it in feasibility (PLAYBOOK 3d) before designing around any original routine you would keep unchanged, speed up or wrap: a copier, a renderer, a sound player, a wait.

question: Does one plot call draw a whole figure, part of one, or one piece of a multi-part object?
summary: Classify every plot entry by what one call draws, before choosing hook sites or a Display check.

question: A figure flashes by being redrawn with a colour override: does each colour cost a separate pattern conversion and cache entry?
summary: Use when the game draws a figure with a colour override (R-Type: 8EB1, one ink for every cell) and the sprite converter keys its cache by graphic + ink.

question: Where does a software polygon renderer's time go on the Next, and which changes (CPU, DMA, blitter) pay?
summary: Profile the whole update by routine in the simulator first; there may be no hot spot (largest 13 %).

question: Do figures show far fewer distinct images than plots, so uploads can be skipped?
summary: Reuse a slot when the same image shows again and the working set fits.

question: Can the ULA keep the scenery's colours when game logic reads the cells the plotter paints?
summary: Keep the original's attribute file in a Next page (the shadow), let the plotter paint only the shadow, and redirect every other attribute reader and writer, so the ULA shows the scenery's colours while logic sees exactly the original's.

question: Can a 4-bit Layer 2 picture (640x256) show more than 16 colours by giving each band of lines its own palette, without seams?
summary: Use for a still picture (title, intro, a "wow" upgrade of an original screen) that needs full horizontal detail and more than 16 colours.

question: When does the new image become visible relative to the original's drawing, and can the viewer see a gap or a half-done state?
summary: Keep the old image visible, build the new one in other pattern memory, then rewrite the sprite attributes in one go, whenever a hook changes a figure that is on screen.

question: Figures move in whole cells once per game update (several frames); can their sprites move a fraction of the step every frame without changing the game?
summary: Use when figures are hardware sprites whose positions change in coarse steps (8 px per 3-9 frames) and the owner wants smooth movement; game logic, collisions and timing stay original.

question: Can the game's own display work be replaced by tilemap / Layer 2 / sprites while its logic, pace and sound stay original?
summary: When the removal experiment (detect.routine-removal) shows a routine's effects are display-only: run the original game logic and producers, take scenery from the game's own map and actors from its own lists, and draw them on Next layers.

question: Can a hook leave interrupts off, or hold them off across the frame's interrupt, when the original would have taken it?
summary: Every hook that disables interrupts and must give the caller's state back: `INCLUDE "lib/hlib_iff.asm"`, `HLIB_IFF_DI` (then PUSH AF) at entry, POP AF + `HLIB_IFF_EI` at every exit.

question: When a faster renderer leaves most of an update's time free, can it show smooth intermediate views without changing the game's speed?
summary: Run the game's own block for an update at 28 MHz inside a pace window, compute the time the original took, draw views between the last camera and the new one while they fit, then show the final view at the original's time.

question: The game ORs a figure's pixels into the screen, then ORs its ink into a rectangle of cells: can sprites show exactly the pixels that ink makes coloured, with no clash on the rest?
summary: Use when one figure is OR-blitted as 1-bit images, then coloured by an ink OR over a cell rectangle, so other pixels in those cells take its colour.

question: Can added hook time let an interrupt land inside a routine the ISR also calls?
summary: Count hook depth and defer the game's interrupt handler to the outermost hook exit, when the handler calls a routine that is not re-entrant and the hooks add time.

question: Does slowly scrolled scenery judder because each 1-pixel step is held for several frames, and can the step be halved without changing the game's speed?
summary: Use when scenery already lives on Layer 2 (patch.hybrid-display-replacement) and moves 1 pixel per game update held for 3+ frames, so the eye sees a start-stop rhythm (R-Type: 1 px per 4 frames).

question: Can the player see the game's loading screen from the moment they press ENTER, without the patch carrying a copy of it?
summary: The loader reads 6,912 bytes at a given offset of the player's own game file straight to the screen when the options are confirmed, then prints "Patching" and one dot per bank built.

question: Can the Next change from the original screen to an upscaled picture with a full-colour effect instead of a hard cut?
summary: Use to move between two still screens at start-up or in a menu: the original's screen and its upscaled "wow" version (`patch.copper-palette-bands` for the picture).

question: Can a game whose view is drawn by a slow software renderer show that view from a Z80N renderer on Layer 2 while its own code still runs?
summary: Run the game's own update and redraw unchanged (buffer and ULA stay whole) and draw the same view again with a Z80N renderer in its own pages, on Layer 2 over the view window.

question: Under the ORIGINAL pace target, does a hook take less time than the code it displaces, so the game would run faster than the original?
summary: Targets: **ORIGINAL** (default), SLOWDOWN REMOVED (owner's choice), TURBO (menu option).

question: Does the game take random numbers from R, so that a hook's different instruction count changes the game?
summary: Default for every NEW engine (owner decision 2026-11-04): with it the same inputs give the original's game, enemies and deaths included, so recordings stay in step and the pace meter compares like with like.

question: Does every hook exit leave the CPU at the speed the game was running at when the hook was entered?
summary: Every NEW engine's hooks: `INCLUDE "lib/hlib_speed.asm"`, `HLIB_SPEED_IN latch` at entry, `HLIB_SPEED_OUT latch` at every exit (ENGINE_CONTRACT "Hook library").

question: How does a painted colour sheet reach sprites whose patterns the hooks build from game graphics at each draw?
summary: Every game is paintable, recolour needs no rebuild (docs/COLOURS.md).

question: Figures pass behind scenery in the original, but the scenery's black paper hides them in whole 8x8 cells: can the black that is open to the sky become transparent without per-frame work?
summary: Use when scenery is drawn on Layer 2 in front of sprites (NR 0x15 Layer 2 over sprites, as the original's owner map makes scenery win) and its black paper shows sprites cut in 8x8 squares.

question: Can the game's plotters draw a figure somewhere the screen never shows, unchanged, so the hook can turn it into a sprite?
summary: Replace the shared CALL target (or entry) that gives the plotters their buffer address, so a converted figure is drawn by the game's own unchanged loop into a scratch copy of the buffer, and build its sprite at the commit.

question: Can a routine that also plays the beeper be accelerated without changing the sound or the game's pace?
summary: When detect.pacing-structure finds that code you need time from also writes the beeper (Inferno's copier: one OUT 254 per cell).

question: Does any ROM byte the game can reach come from the Next's own ROM instead of the build?
summary: Every build that hooks through the alt ROM.

question: Can added work run inside a timed window without moving its deadlines, and what happens when it does not fit?
summary: When a window has idle time between deadlines (OUT times, a pad) and the hook has work that can be split: run the work as a coroutine in slices, each started only with enough ticks to the next deadline.

question: Can figures become sprites without changing a single screen byte the game reads?
summary: Leave the plotter writing the ULA exactly as the original, and put hardware sprites exactly on each figure's ink pixels, in front.

question: Can XOR-drawn figures leave the ULA while the original screen stays exactly recoverable?
summary: Send converted XOR writes to a 1-bit shadow screen instead of the ULA, so ULA ^ shadow equals the original screen at every moment, and show figures from the shadow (Layer 2) or per-image sprites.

question: Does any video frame show the new sprites over the old screen, a figure missing, or a cell colour for one frame only?
summary: Use on every build the user tests that switches sprites at a commit point or keeps figure cells on the ULA (PLAYBOOK 6b): the differential verifiers compare state at hook returns and frame ends, so they pass a build whose picture is wrong BETWEEN two such points.

question: Does the verifier's model of what the figures drew explain the original screen exactly?
summary: A verifier that checks the patched screen against a model (background + figures) can pass when the model and the hook share a wrong assumption: both forget a writer.

question: Does every colour boundary of an Enhanced set sit on a line the artist drew, or where the drawn shape narrows, and never straight across a flat area?
summary: Every new Enhanced colour set: `python -m nexclash.paint regions` then `paint` (docs/COLOURS.md PAINTER) before any hand work.

question: How does an agent see a display bug that appears only at one event (a power-up, a boss) without playing by hand?
summary: Use for display checks of a build (sprites, scenery, glide, colours) at a scene the recording or random play rarely reaches.

question: How is a rewritten routine (renderer, maths) shown equal to the original beyond the inputs a recording happens to hold?
summary: Split the original into stages at fixed PCs, capture each stage's input and output from the recording, and gate the port at every stage and end to end.

question: Does the build play the same game work in the same time as the original, in quiet and in busy scenes?
summary: Use on every build the user tests whose hooks add time (PLAYBOOK 6b): games without frame sync slow down by the hook time, and a frame-synced game slows once a busy frame overruns.
